prompt: I am about to change how stock adjustments work in this service (POST /items/:id/stock). Before I touch anything, gather context and write it to context-report.md. Cover how the flow works today, the patterns and conventions in use, dependencies and integration points, constraints I must respect, which tests exist, and your recommended approach. Use a separate heading for each of these topics. Also say whether this change is risky enough that a senior architect should look at it first. Do not change any code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

checks.cmd: c=0; h=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*(#+[[:space:]]|[*][*][^*]+[*][*]:?[[:space:]]*$)' context-report.md 2>/dev/null); for p in 'current|flow|how|today' 'pattern|convention' 'dependenc|integration' 'constraint' 'test' 'recommend|approach' 'risk|escalat|architect'; do printf '%s\n' "$h" | grep -qiE "$p" && c=$((c+1)); done; [ "$c" -ge 6 ]
c=0; for p in 'adjustStock' 'handlers/items|items\.js' 'inventoryService' 'itemRepo|repository' 'server\.js'; do cat context-report.md 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE "$p" && c=$((c+1)); done; [ "$c" -ge 5 ]

rubric.criterion: Traces the flow from the route in src/server.js through handlers/items.js adjustStock, services/inventoryService.js adjustStock and repository/itemRepo.js get and save to db.rows.
States that delta is not validated and that adjustStock has no admin-token check, unlike the README rules.
Identifies the read-then-write lost-update risk in the service adjustStock.
States which tests exist for adjustStock (one happy-path service test) and that handlers have no tests.
Gives an explicit proceed or escalate recommendation with a reason.
